opening.argument: The pitch ties BYDFi signups and deposits to a $1,000 bonus for depositing $5,000, a displayed "$2,000 BONUS," and deposit-based reward tiers. It then urges viewers to recruit depositors, claiming that friends' deposits can generate hundreds of dollars per day and one large depositor can produce thousands. Signup and UID submission are linked to VIP access and partner benefits. These incentives establish a recruitment-and-commission scheme: the appeal rests on depositing funds and bringing others into the arrangement. The speaker calls it affiliate marketing and claims substantial account earnings, but those claims supply no verification of the account, bonus delivery, commission terms, profitability, or transaction outcome. The deposit incentives and recruitment-driven income promises support the finding of a scam without establishing actual losses.
